tasks.question: Where does binary quadratic model data flow through the encoding, compression, and upload pipeline during problem submission to D-Wave cloud solvers?
tasks.reference_answer: The compressed BQM path is UnstructuredSolver.upload_bqm: it first tries a file view, then for serializable BQMs falls back to encode_problem_as_bq(..., compress=True), and passes encoded data to client.upload_problem_encoded (dwave/cloud/solver.py:418-448). The fallback converts to serializable JSON, ASCII-encodes it and zlib-compresses it (dwave/cloud/coders.py:270-303). Multipart parts are submitted through the upload-part executor (dwave/cloud/client.py:1860-1878). After upload, the solver submits a bqm-ref body using the returned problem ID (dwave/cloud/solver.py:345-356). Structured qp encoding is a separate path.

tasks.question: Why does the current simple token-based authentication architecture in dwave-cloud-client create scalability bottlenecks when handling concurrent API requests across multiple thread pools?
tasks.reference_answer: create_session creates an isolated session and adds self.token as X-Auth-Token (dwave/cloud/client.py:506-530). This source shows static header-based authentication; it does not establish that sharing the same token value across sessions serializes requests or limits scalability. A missing refresh mechanism may require external credential replacement if credentials become invalid, but identifying a concurrent throughput bottleneck would require measurements and server-side behavior beyond this code.
